subject: Computer Networking
title: The Dot-Com Boom and Bust
description: A fast breakdown of The Dot-Com Boom and Bust for builders.

hook.text: In the late 1990s, adding '.com' to your company name doubled your stock price. The hype was surreal.

buildup.text: Investors poured billions into web startups. Business models didn't matter — 'get big fast' was the only strategy.

discovery.text: Companies like Amazon, eBay, and Google launched during this era. So did Pets.com, Webvan, and Kozmo.

twist.text: The bubble burst in 2000. The NASDAQ lost 78% of its value. Hundreds of dot-coms vanished overnight.

climax.text: The survivors — Amazon, Google, eBay — went on to dominate the global economy for decades.

punchline.text: The bubble was wrong about timing, not about the internet's potential.

quiz.question: What happened to the NASDAQ during the dot-com bust?
options: It lost about 78% of its value

details.summary: The dot-com bubble of the late 1990s saw massive investment in internet companies based on growth rather than profit. The NASDAQ peaked in March 2000 and then crashed, wiping out trillions of dollars.
details.whyItMatters: The dot-com era established the internet as a commercial platform. The survivors built the infrastructure and business models that power today's digital economy.
takeaways: Speculative investment inflated internet company valuations
The NASDAQ crashed in 2000, destroying trillions in value
Survivors like Amazon and eBay became internet giants

faq.question: What caused the dot-com bubble to burst?
faq.answer: Companies with no revenue or path to profitability received massive valuations based on growth metrics alone. When investors demanded profits, most companies could not deliver. The resulting sell-off cascaded through the market, destroying both legitimate and speculative companies.

faq.question: What lasting impact did the dot-com era have?
faq.answer: It built massive fiber optic infrastructure that the internet still uses. It established e-commerce, online advertising, and software-as-a-service as viable businesses. The surviving companies became today's tech giants. The fiber laid during the boom enabled broadband adoption.
